articles.title: Thai Queen makes first solo flight in fighter jet
articles.summary: Thailand’s Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.
articles.body:
Thailand's Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The Queen was shown boarding a Gripen on 8 October at an airfield in Surat Thani province, southern Thailand, while King Maha Vajiralongkorn watched from the ground.

The Royal Household has said she is an experienced pilot, having logged about 1,188 hours across several types of aircraft since she began flying in 2010.

She also co-piloted aircraft carrying the King on official visits to other countries, the Royal Household said.

articles.title: Segundo terremoto de magnitude 6,6 atinge o Panamá | G1
articles.standfirst: O novo abalo ocorre na esteira de uma série de tremores secundários que se seguiram ao primeiro tremor, de magnitude 7,7. Mais de 10 réplicas foram sentidas entre o primeiro e o segundo terremoto.
articles.summary: O novo abalo ocorre na esteira de uma série de tremores secundários que se seguiram ao primeiro tremor, de magnitude 7,7.
articles.body:
Um segundo forte terremoto de magnitude 6,6 atingiu o Panamá nesta sexta-feira (9), informou o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS, na sigla em inglês). O novo abalo ocorre na esteira de uma série de tremores secundários que se seguiram ao primeiro tremor, de magnitude 7,7 .

A profundidade do segundo tremor foi de 10 quilômetros e ocorreu em terra, na região de Río Grande, no oeste do país.

Segundo boletim do Sistema Nacional de Proteção Civil do Panamá, não há mortes confirmadas, mas há registro de feridos encaminhados a hospitais. As províncias mais afetadas são Coclé, Veraguas e Los Santos, segundo o órgão.

Terremotos no Panamá — Foto: Editoria de Arte/g1

O tremor foi fortemente sentido na Cidade do Panamá e na vizinha Costa Rica, segundo o Serviço Geológico dos EUA (USGS, na sigla em inglês). O epicentro ocorreu em terra, no sul do país, na comunidade rural de La Pitaloza, uma área pouco povoada .

A profundidade do tremor foi rasa, de 12 quilômetros da superfície , o que aumenta a intensidade em terra. Há relatos de edifícios e torres parcialmente colapsados no sul ( leia mais abaixo ).

Um alerta por risco de tsunami chegou a ser ativado para a costa do Pacífico, mas depois foi retirado.

Incialmente, o USGS havia registrado uma magnitude de 8,0, mas depois revisou a intensidade para 7,7.

O terremoto aconteceu às 14h56 pelo horário de Brasília. Cerca de meia hora depois, um segundo tremor, de magnitude 5,5, também foi registrado mais a sul do país, na localidade de Bajo Corral. Ao todo, foram registradas ao menos 6 réplicas .

Ainda não havia informações sobre vítimas até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Pelas redes sociais, moradores e a imprensa do país mostravam cenas de destruição.

Na cidade de Penonomé, uma das mais atingidas, parte de um hotel colapsou ( veja acima );

Na cidade de Santiago, a imprensa local afirmou que a torre de uma catedral veio abaixo;

Em diversas províncias do sul, aulas foram suspensas;

Na cidade de Colón, perto do Canal do Panamá , um grande incêndio atingiu instalações do porto. A Autoridade do Canal informou que a hidrovia seguia operando normalmente, apesar do tremor.

O aeroporto da Cidade do Panamá, capital do país, foi fechado por precaução. Imagens mostraram pessoas na pista do aeroporto após o tremor.

Brasileiros relatam 'susto grande' e 'gritaria'

A jornalista brasileira Laís Gomes e o marido foram surpreendidos pelo tremor na Cidade do Panamá. O casal estava em um restaurante no momento do terremoto e sentiram a mesa e as cadeiras balançarem. "Todo mundo começou a gritar", relatou Laís . O local foi rapidamente esvaziado.

O guia turístico brasileiro Roque Freitas, que mora há 16 anos na capital panamenha, diz que o tremor foi um grande susto. Ele relata que há registros de queda de marquises no Casco Antiguo , centro histórico da capital.

Pessoas saem às ruas na Cidade do Panamá após o terremoto de magnitude de 7,7 que atingiu o país em 9 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Enea Lebrun/ Reuters

articles.title: Moradores reclamam da falta de água em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo moradores, problema tem afetado atividades básicas, como banho, preparo de alimentos e limpeza da casa.
articles.summary: Segundo moradores, problema tem afetado atividades básicas, como banho, preparo de alimentos e limpeza da casa.
articles.body:
Moradores de Carabuçu, distrito de Bom Jesus do Itabapoana , no Noroeste Fluminense, estão enfrentando problemas com o abastecimento de água. Segundo relatos, algumas casas estão há pelo menos cinco dias sem água.

A falta de abastecimento tem dificultado tarefas básicas do dia a dia, como tomar banho, lavar a casa e cozinhar.

Em uma das residências, uma moradora mostrou que praticamente não há água saindo da torneira.

“Não tem nenhuma gota d’água. A torneira só está com um fiapo de água. Não tem uma gota d’água”, contou.

A situação também preocupa porque há idosos entre os moradores afetados. Dona Cremilda, de 67 anos, contou que precisou recorrer a outras fontes para conseguir água para as necessidades básicas da casa.

“Trouxe da roça essa água que está aqui pra gente usar, pra jogar no banheiro e na cozinha. Água da torneira não tem. Pra beber a água, a gente tem que pegar lá embaixo, na casa do meu filho.”

Segundo ela, até mesmo a água usada para outras tarefas precisou ser buscada fora de casa.

“Uma gota de água. Não tem uma gota. Com a casa cheia de gente, nenhuma gota d’água.”

Outro problema relatado pelos moradores é a dificuldade para conseguir água potável. Em alguns casos, familiares precisam buscar água em outros pontos para garantir o consumo.

A CEDAE, Companhia Estadual de Águas e Esgotos do Rio de Janeiro, é responsável pelo abastecimento de água em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, a CEDAE não havia informado o motivo da falta de água registrada atualmente em Carabuçu nem apresentado previsão para a normalização do abastecimento.

Em alguns casos, familiares precisam buscar água em outros pontos para garantir o consumo. — Foto: Blog Alan Gonçalves

articles.title: Incêndio atinge casa no Centro de Campina Grande | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, quintal da casa estava com vegetação alta e também com pneus. Fogo pegou esse material, mas foi controlado por vizinhos e, posteriormente, pela corporação.
articles.summary: De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, quintal da casa estava com vegetação alta e também com pneus. Fogo pegou esse material, mas foi controlado por vizinhos e, posteriormente, pela corporação.
articles.body:
Incêndio atinge casa no Centro de Campina Grande — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Um incêndio atingiu uma casa no bairro do Centro, em Campina Grande, nesta sexta-feira (9). De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, o que pegou fogo foi uma vegetação que estava alta no local e também pneus no quintal da casa. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Também conforme o Corpo de Bombeiros, a fumaça ficou muito alta, no entanto, além da queima da vegetação e dos pneus, nada mais foi atingido. As chamas foram controladas, inicialmente, por vizinhos, com baldes de água e, posteriormente, com o trabalho dos agentes.

Ainda não se sabe o que causou o fogo. Uma perícia deve ser feita para saber os motivos.

articles.title: Motorista perde o controle da direção e carro cai em ribeirão | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a motorista, de 58 anos, sofreu ferimentos no braço. O acidente ocorreu na tarde de quinta-feira (8), no bairro Santa Catarina, em Fartura (SP).
articles.summary: Uma mulher de 58 anos perdeu o controle da direção e caiu com o carro em um ribeirão, após desviar de uma batida em Fartura (SP), na tarde de quinta-feira (8).
articles.body:
Mulher cai com carro em ribeirão de Fartura, na quinta-feira (8) — Foto: Portal do Sudoeste Paulista/Reprodução

Uma mulher de 58 anos perdeu o controle da direção e caiu com o carro em um ribeirão no bairro Santa Catarina, em Fartura (SP), na tarde de quinta-feira (8).

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a motorista relatou que seguia pela Rua Samuel de Oliveira, no sentido do centro para o bairro, quando no cruzamento com a Rua Osvaldo Lucarelli, virou à esquerda, pois ia acessar uma ponte improvisada no local.

Ainda conforme o relato, assim que virou, teve carro "fechado" por um outro veículo e, para evitar a batida, acabou desviando. Nesse momento, ela perdeu o controle da direção, desceu a rua e caiu no ribeirão.

A vítima foi socorrida por moradores que a ajudaram a sair do carro. Ela sofreu um pequeno ferimento no braço esquerdo e relatou dores no corpo dolorido devido ao impacto.

À polícia, ela apontou que o automóvel dela ficou com a lateral esquerda, o vidro traseiro e o para-choque dianteiro danificados.

articles.title: 'Todos começaram a gritar', diz brasileira sobre terremoto no Panamá | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta sexta-feira, o país foi atingido por um forte terremoto de magnitude 7,7. Um alerta por risco de tsunami foi ativado para quase toda a costa do Pacífico da América Central.
articles.summary: Nesta sexta-feira, o país foi atingido por um forte terremoto de magnitude 7,7. Um alerta por risco de tsunami foi ativado para quase toda a costa do Pacífico da América Central.
articles.body:
A jornalista brasileira Laís Gomes e o marido foram surpreendidos pelo tremor que atingiu o Panamá nesta sexta-feira (9). Eles tão no país para passar o feriado e tinham acabado de chegar a um restaurante em Casco Viejo, na Cidade do Panamá, quando o tremor começou.

"Eu e meu marido sentamos em uma bancada e eu estava olhando o cardápio. Eu não senti quando começou [o tremor], achei que era a cadeira balançando. E aí ele [o marido] falou: 'Tá balançando', e nisso que ele falou que estava balançando, a mesa começou a dançar quase", conta.

Nesta sexta-feira, o Panamá foi atingido por um forte terremoto de magnitude 7,7 que atingiu o sul do país. Um alerta por risco de tsunami foi ativado para quase toda a costa do Pacífico da América Central.

Laís Gomes e o marido estavam no Panamá no momento do terremoto de 7,7 magnitudes. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Segundo Laís, uma gritaria se seguiu ao tremor, e todos foram orientados a evacuar o restaurante.

Outros comércios e estabelecimentos da região também foram evacuados.

A jornalista conta que, apesar do susto e do forte tremor, não parece ter havido danos em prédios da região e nem houve relatos de feridos nas imediações do restaurante onde estava.

De acordo com ela, viaturas e carros de bombeiros passaram pelo local.

Terremoto de magnitude 7,6 atinge o Panamá — Foto: Reprodução

O forte terremoto de magnitude 7,7 que atingiu o sul do Panamá nesta sexta-feira (9) foi sentido em diversas regiões do país, incluindo a capital, e levou à emissão de alertas de tsunami para países de toda a costa do Pacífico.

O tremor ocorreu a apenas 12 quilômetros de profundidade, uma característica que costuma aumentar a intensidade dos abalos sentidos na superfície.

Inicialmente, o terremoto chegou a ser registrado com magnitude 8,0, mas o valor foi revisado posteriormente pelos especialistas para 7,7 após a análise de novos dados coletados por estações sismológicas.

Pessoas vão para as ruas após forte terremoto atingir o Panamá — Foto: Arnulo Fanco/AFP

O episódio reacendeu uma dúvida comum sempre que um grande tremor ocorre em alguma parte do mundo: afinal, o que significa um terremoto dessa magnitude na prática?

Em linhas gerais, um terremoto na faixa de 7,0 a 7,9 é considerado de grande porte e tem potencial para provocar danos graves, incluindo o desabamento de edificações, danos à infraestrutura e destruição em áreas habitadas.

Mas a magnitude, sozinha, não conta toda a história. A profundidade do tremor, a distância do epicentro até cidades e o tipo de solo da região estão entre os fatores que ajudam a determinar o tamanho real dos impactos.

👉 Um exemplo de país acostumado a conviver com esse tipo de fenômeno é o Japão . Localizado no chamado Anel de Fogo do Pacífico, uma região marcada pelo encontro de placas tectônicas e intensa atividade geológica, o país registra tremores constantemente e concentra cerca de 20% dos terremotos de magnitude igual ou superior a 6 registrados no planeta.

articles.title: Chuva e ventania destelham igreja em Lorena | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporal também deixou estragos em outras três cidades da região.
articles.summary: Temporal também deixou estragos em outras três cidades da região.
articles.body:
Temporal destelha igreja em Lorena — Foto: Gabriel Guimarães/TV Vanguarda

Um temporal atingiu Lorena na tarde desta sexta-feira (9). A força do vento acabou destelhando a Igreja São Pedro Apóstolo, no bairro Olaria.

A ventania começou por volta das 16h30. A Defesa Civil de São Paulo emitiu um alerta sobre o temporal na cidade. O aviso tratava sobre raios, vento forte e possibilidade de granizo.

Logo no início da temporal, a força do vento tirou o telhado da igreja. Uma parte da cobertura ficou presa nos fios e outra caiu na rua. Não há registro de feridos.

Outros bairros da cidade como Santo Antônio, Industrial e bairro da Cruz também registraram ocorrências como queda de árvore e pontos de alagamento.

Em nota, a prefeitura de Lorena afirmou que está atuando com mais de 20 profissionais nas ruas, além de duas máquinas e seis caminhões.

A Defesa Civil segue realizando vistorias e atendendo aos chamados da população. Devido ao grande número de ocorrências e à continuidade dos trabalhos, ainda não foi possível concluir um balanço dos danos registrados.

Em São José dos Campos, moradores registraram chuva de granizo na região da Vila Ema . Na zona sul, houve alagamentos na Avenida Cidade Jardim, perto do shopping Vale Sul, na Avenida Andrômeda, no cruzamento com a Avenida Iguape, e no Jardim das Indústrias.

Árvore que caiu na Ouro Fino, em São José. — Foto: Bruna Capasciutti/TV Vanguarda

A Avenida Ouro Fino, na zona sul, também ficou alagada e uma árvore caiu . Já na Avenida Nove de Julho, outra árvore caiu e obstruiu a faixa da esquerda. No Anel Viário, o acúmulo de água dificultou a passagem dos veículos.

Em Campos do Jordão, uma grande quantidade de granizo caiu nas proximidades do Horto Florestal , no bairro Descansópolis. As pedras de gelo cobriram telhados e gramados.

Temporal provoca alagamentos, queda de árvores e granizo em cidades do Vale do Paraíba e região — Foto: Foto 1: Ana Jully | Foto 2: Diogo Souza | Foto 3: Paty Martins

Em Jacareí, moradores do Jardim Luiza registraram chuva de granizo . A Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta para chuva forte e persistente na região, com raios, ventos e granizo, e informou que o temporal também atingia municípios vizinhos. O órgão orientou a população a procurar abrigo.

Na Rodovia Presidente Dutra, no trecho de São José dos Campos, o trânsito ficou parado no sentido Rio de Janeiro durante a chuva.

articles.title: VÍDEO mostra enxurrada de água e lama invadindo ruas no Chile | G1
articles.standfirst: Fortes chuvas inundaram avenidas e arrastaram veículos em Las Condes, na região metropolitana de Santiago.
articles.summary: VÍDEO mostra enxurrada de água e lama invadindo ruas no Chile; país decretou calamidade
articles.body:
O governo do Chile declarou nesta sexta-feira (9) a região de Las Condes, distrito da capital Santiago, como zona de desastre, após chuvas provocarem enchentes repentinas e deslizamentos de terra. Ao menos 6 pessoas ficaram feridas e várias áreas foram evacuadas.

A declaração de calamidade permite que órgãos públicos adotem medidas extraordinárias para coordenar a assistência emergencial, avaliar os danos e apoiar os esforços de recuperação, segundo a imprensa local.

As fortes chuvas de quinta fizeram com que grandes volumes de água e lama invadissem as ruas, arrastassem veículos e inundassem residências em Las Condes - uma das áreas mais nobres e de maior poder aquisitivo da região metropolitana de Santiago. Imagens impressionantes mostram o momento em que uma enxurrada de lama invade as ruas ( assista acima ).

O Rio Mapocho também transbordou, enquanto as inundações tornaram estradas intransitáveis e levaram equipes de emergência a responder a diversos pedidos de ajuda.

Pessoas protegem com tábuas as janelas quebradas de uma loja de conveniência OXXO após fortes chuvas provocarem um deslizamento de terra em Las Condes, em Santiago, no Chile. — Foto: Ailen Diaz/Reuters

A prefeita de Las Condes, Catalina San Martín, afirmou que 14,4 centímetros de chuva foram registrados nos últimos dias, cerca de nove vezes a média histórica para o mês de outubro. Segundo ela, o solo ficou saturado, aumentando o risco de novos alagamentos e deslizamentos.

Pelo menos seis pessoas ficaram feridas , entre elas uma criança de um ano que sofreu fraturas. Bombeiros resgataram ou evacuaram mais de mil pessoas. As equipes de emergência seguem trabalhando para remover entulhos e restabelecer o acesso às áreas atingidas.

O Serviço Nacional de Prevenção a Desastres do Chile também decretou alerta vermelho para 10 municípios localizados em áreas montanhosas da Região Metropolitana de Santiago devido ao risco de novos deslizamentos.

articles.title: Cadu de Lula inicia campanha de 2º turno com caminhada em Natal | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT esteve acompanhado da vice, Larissa Rosado, e defendeu continuidade de políticas do governo estadual.
articles.summary: Cadu de Lula iniciou a agenda de rua do segundo turno das Eleições 2026 no Rio Grande do Norte com caminhada em Natal ao lado da vice Larissa Rosado.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte Cadu de Lula (PT) fez uma caminhada pelo bairro das Quintas, na Zona Oeste de Natal , na tarde desta sexta-feira (9). Acompanhado da candidata a vice-governadora, Larissa Rosado (PSB), de correligionários e apoiadores, ele conversou com moradores e ouviu demandas de comerciantes.

A atividade marcou o início das mobilizações de rua da campanha de Cadu no segundo turno. O candidato afirmou que pretende manter a estratégia de percorrer comunidades e conversar diretamente com a população, como fez durante o primeiro turno.

Durante a caminhada, Cadu defendeu a continuidade de políticas implementadas pelo governo da professora Fátima Bezerra (PT), do qual fez parte, e afirmou que pretende ampliar as ações em um eventual mandato.

Entre as prioridades citadas estão a geração de emprego e renda, a redução das desigualdades sociais e a melhoria dos serviços públicos, principalmente nas áreas de saúde, segurança, educação e assistência social.

Ao falar sobre a nova etapa da campanha, o candidato disse que pretende apresentar propostas voltadas às diferentes regiões da capital e do interior do estado.

Cadu de Lula fez campanha nas Quintas, em Natal — Foto: Inter TV Cabugi

"A gente está começando essa caminhada no segundo turno aqui, da melhor forma possível aqui nas Quintas, uma região da cidade de Natal, que a gente tem que trabalhar ainda mais para desenvolver essa região. A gente tem propostas para todas as regiões da cidade, para todas as regiões do Estado, e a gente está aqui hoje para iniciar essa caminhada no segundo turno, fazendo o que a gente fez durante todo o primeiro turno, conversando com as pessoas, indo de casa a casa, conversando com o nosso povo, mostrando que o nosso projeto tem conexão com a realidade do nosso povo."

Cadu também afirmou que pretende dar continuidade às políticas implementadas durante a atual gestão estadual, com foco no desenvolvimento econômico e na geração de empregos.

"O nosso projeto é um projeto de avanço. Eu tenho muito orgulho de ter participado do governo da professora Fátima, mas o nosso projeto é um projeto de avanço nas políticas que a gente implantou, implementou no governo da professora Fátima. A gente vai dar ao Rio Grande do Norte um projeto de desenvolvimento, geração de emprego".

O candidato Allyson Bezerra (União) não teve agenda pública de campanha nesta sexta-feira (9).

articles.title: Swinney backs Flynn in ferry gas leak row and says 'Nobody's perfect'
articles.summary: The first minister says he has confidence in his transport secretary, who denies being briefed about the ferry incident.
articles.body:
First Minister John Swinney has backed Stephen Flynn in the row over whether the transport secretary had been briefed about a gas leak on a CalMac ferry.

Speaking to the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg programme in an interview to be broadcast on Sunday, Swinney said emails showed Flynn had not been briefed ahead of a Holyrood committee meeting last month.

The first minister said he had confidence in his transport secretary, who "recognised that he should have been across an issue to be in front of the transport committee and he remedied that right away".

Swinney added: "Nobody's perfect, nobody's infallible".

Flynn was appearing before the transport committee on 9 September when he said he was not aware of a BBC Scotland News story published online more than nine hours earlier.

It revealed how a faulty valve led to 700kg of flammable methane gas being vented from the side of the ferry MV Glen Sannox while it was carrying passengers from Arran to Troon in June 2025.

Valve failure on CalMac ferry saw uncontrolled escape of flammable gas

Speaking to the committee, Flynn said he had missed the report because he was facetiming his children before the meeting.

But a briefing document released via a freedom of information (FOI) request and published by the Scottish Sun and The Times newspapers on Thursday evening showed Flynn's office was contacted about the story twice in the half hour before the committee meeting began.

Flynn later appeared to be blindsided when committee members quizzed him about the story.

As Swinney backed his cabinet secretary on Friday, Flynn insisted that media reports that he had received a briefing before his committee appearance were false.

He wrote on X: "This is not true. I should've seen the BBC news that morning - but the FOI confirms I was not briefed.

"Jeez, if I'd known, I'd have given a damn sight better answer than I did at the time!

"An answer that wasn't acceptable and nobody was more frustrated than myself about that."

Transport Scotland said the documents released this week "made clear" Flynn had "not been briefed on the issue" before his committee appearance, and the emails sent to his office had not been shared with him.

The director of ferries at Transport Scotland, Chris Wilcock - who appeared at the committee alongside Flynn - was aware of the BBC story about the gas leak.

Another document obtained by the Sun shows that Wilcock emailed other Transport Scotland officials at 08:13 - more than an hour before the committee meeting began - asking for "lines on the BBC story last night about the gas escape".

The Sun report concentrated on emails sent by Flynn's office at 17:04 on 9 September, hours after his committee appearance, The paper said they were evidence of attempts to "cover-up" the minister's lack of preparedness.

One email - now seen by BBC Scotland - says the attached statement had been "cleared by Mr Flynn".

Quoting Flynn, it says: "I was not briefed on this incident, however details were shared with the former cabinet secretary for transport on 30 June 2025, in line with agreed processes."

Reacting to the publication of that email, transport committee convener Willie Rennie told BBC Scotland Flynn was "only making things worse for himself".

"What is alarming is that he seems to have attempted a cover-up, dragging in officials and Transport Scotland," he said.

"And if he had bothered to listen to the news in the morning before the committee session he would not have been surprised by my questions about the leaking of flammable gas on the Glen Sannox."

Scottish Conservative leader Russell Findlay demanded Flynn refer himself to the independent advisers on the ministerial code.

"Stephen Flynn should have admitted that he had simply failed to do his job properly," he said.

"But instead, this bombshell new evidence suggests that he conspired with officials to execute a sleekit, skin-saving cover-up."

A Transport Scotland spokesperson said: "As the timestamp notes, a draft media statement was sent to Mr Flynn's office shortly before he arrived at the committee and this was not shared with him.

"A high-level media statement does not constitute formal briefing, which the cabinet secretary received later. The previous cabinet secretary for transport [Fiona Hyslop] was briefed on the issue last year, at the time of the incident."

A "ministerial engagement briefing" issued ahead of the transport committee's meeting on 9 September showed two emails sent to Flynn at 08:48 and 09:04.

The meeting - which marked Flynn's first appearance before the committee since becoming transport secretary in May - was scheduled to get under way at 09:15.

The initial email was sent to Flynn and Transport Scotland officials.

It acknowledges Transport Scotland was "yet to be contacted for comment".

However, it includes a suggested comment from policy officials "if the coverage prompts any questions at committee".

A follow-up, sent 16 minutes later, includes a comment from CalMac and was sent to Flynn and Transport Scotland officials "for awareness".

The transport secretary was questioned about the gas incident – which came to light after an FOI by BBC Scotland – by committee convener Rennie later that morning.

Flynn told Rennie he had not been given a briefing about the story though he quickly clarified "unless I've missed it".

He added: "I wasn't listening or watching the BBC this morning convener... I didn't see the news because I was facetiming my kids - but that is a different matter."

Flynn said "it may have been the case" that the incident "may have been conveyed" to him as part of a wider tranche of documents he was given when he took over the role from predecessor Fiona Hyslop.

He later clarified that Hyslop had been told about the leak.

Speaking to Kuenssberg in a pre-recorded interview on Friday afternoon, Swinney said: "Obviously, Stephen Flynn recognised that he should have been across an issue to be in front of the transport committee and he remedied that right away."

He added: "The material had not been passed to him so he had not seen it before he got to committee and he remedied it later on with the response that he gave to the transport committee."

Swinney said it was obvious Flynn had not seen the email exchange between officials that morning.

Asked whether that was "good enough", he responded "nobody's perfect, nobody's infallible. So Stephen Flynn, when he realised that he had, he was not across that issue, remedied that with the transport committee later on."

Swinney said the men had talked about the issue and, asked whether he had confidence in Flynn, answered: "Yes I do, yes."

The latest exchange came just a few days after Swinney defended Flynn at a separate committee meeting.

Willie Rennie raised "serious concerns about his [Flynn's] competence as a minister" and questioned his "awareness of his brief".

Swinney said he "respectfully disagreed" with Rennie's analysis, adding he was confident all his ministers were "across their responsibilities".

Glen Sannox, the first UK-built ship with engines capable of being directly powered by liquefied natural gas (LNG) , has a dual duel propulsion system supplied and commissioned by the Finnish firm Wartsila.

Some engine problems emerged during a crossing from Troon to Brodick on the Isle of Arran on 3 June 2025 - and on the return leg a valve that was part of the engine system failed, leading to gas being vented out the side of the ship.

The engines, it later emerged, had been supplied by Wartsila without certain failsafe monitoring systems, meaning the crew were initially unaware the valve had failed.

Gas continued to leak from the ship for 12 minutes before the crew realised what was happening and were able to close the valve manually.

So much gas was released that some was sucked back into the engine rooms through ventilation shafts, triggering gas detector alarms.

CalMac immediately suspended the use of LNG until the failsafe systems were installed, and for operational reasons the ship has not run on gas since the incident.

An investigation also revealed the engine manufacturer had previously recommended a reliability upgrade to the valve that failed, but it is unclear if these warnings were passed on to the Ferguson shipyard which built the ship.

articles.title: A WWII airfield once used by Britain's famous Dambusters was later quarried for sand; today its runway is a nature reserve filled with skylarks and birds of prey
articles.summary: Woodhall Spa Airfield was constructed on former farmland as a satellite station to RAF Coningsby and opened in February 1942.
articles.body: Woodhall Spa Airfield was constructed on former farmland as a satellite station to RAF Coningsby and opened in February 1942. It was home to several RAF squadrons during the Second World War, including 617 ‘Dambusters’ Squadron, which used the ‘bouncing bomb’ developed by Barnes Wallis to destroy three major dams in the Ruhr. The site was later a sand and gravel quarry. The Trust concluded the final phase of its purchase on 19 September 2014, supported by £450,000 from WREN’s Biodiversity Action Fund and a £100,000 legacy. The reserve has sandy soils, acid grassland, heathland and open water.How did the WWII Dambusters airfield become a nature reserveAccording to Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, Woodhall Spa Airfield was constructed on former farmland as a satellite station to RAF Coningsby and opened in February 1942. The Trust states that, during the Second World War, the airfield was home to several RAF squadrons, including the famous 617 'Dambusters' Squadron.The Trust's reserve page names several other squadrons that served there. It says 97 Squadron and 619 Squadron were heavily involved in the early operations of the Avro Lancaster bomber. It adds that 627 Squadron crucially developed a method of low-level target marking that proved extremely successful.Who led Britain's famous Dambusters raidThe most famous squadron to serve at RAF Woodhall was 617 'Dambusters' Squadron, which was based there for most of the Second World War. The Trust says it was this squadron that used the 'bouncing bomb' developed by Barnes Wallis to destroy three major dams in the Ruhr industrial region of Germany.The Trust's 2014 news release also records a link to Guy Gibson, leader of the Dambusters raid. According to the release, Gibson continued flying missions over Europe after the 1943 raid, until his last flight in 1944. The Trust states that he took off from RAF Woodhall Spa on 19 September 1944 on a mission over Germany, and that his plane was lost whilst returning.How did the former RAF airfield become a nature reserveThe Trust says the airfield was, more recently, used as a sand and gravel quarry. In its news release of 19 September 2014, it announced that it had concluded the final phase of its purchase of the former RAF base. According to the release, £450,000 was donated by WREN's Biodiversity Action Fund Land Purchase Programme, and a further £100,000 came as a legacy donation from Robert Thomas Pearson. The Trust also received substantial public donations. The release notes that the purchase came exactly 70 years after the last flight of Guy Gibson.It would now begin developing the former airfield into a nature reserve. It also said the airfield would be closed for the foreseeable future while machinery from the quarry was removed and development work began. The reserve would be part of a local Living Landscape, connecting existing nature reserves and habitats and allowing wildlife to move through these spaces.How is the former Dambusters airfield being restoredWoodhall Spa Airfield is a landscape of sandy soils with acid grassland, heathland with some marsh areas and open water. The 2014 release set out plans to restore parts of the land to the way it existed in the nineteenth century, including lowland heath, a habitat that already exists in the neighbouring Kirkby Moor nature reserve. It says a record of the landscape in 1890 survives in the diary of the Victorian naturalist Joseph Burtt Davy, who recorded the habitats and wildlife he met around Woodhall Spa. The Trust stated that the reserve would retain the outline of the airfield landing strip while restoring the landscape to its earlier condition. The reserve page includes a photograph of wildfowl flying above a lake in winter.The site has a car park and viewing areas, with limited access and no dogs. It also describes a new memorial garden near the reserve entrance, which it calls "a place of peace and reflection for everyone". The Trust says the garden is intended especially for older or less able visitors, and for veterans who find the walk to the existing war memorial too far. The fundraising target was exceeded, work began, and a new sculpture was installed in time for a visit by the 617 Squadron Association on 18 May 2025, held to commemorate the 80th anniversary of VE Day.You use AI every day. articles.title: Durga Puja pandal count up in Bangladesh, Hindus say ‘reduced fear’
articles.summary: There is cautious optimism among Bangladesh’s minority Hindu community ahead of this year’s Durga Puja.
articles.body: There is cautious optimism among Bangladesh’s minority Hindu community ahead of this year’s Durga Puja. Amid reduced fear after security assurances by the govt, the number of pandals has risen to 33,851 — up 1,460 from last year.Basudeb Dhar, president of Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad (BPUP), the country’s prominent non-political, social and religious organisation representing the community, told TOI from Dhaka on Friday that they were not experiencing the same “sense of fear” which had clouded their festivities the past two years.“In the past two years, our festivities faced ban threats from some right-wing groups. There were provocative social media posts and public rallies against celebrations. This year, the situation is different. BNP-led govt wants the community to celebrate with freedom and fervour. They want to showcase Bangladesh’s diversity and rich cultural heritage before the world,” added Dhar.Dhar attended a high-level meeting chaired by home minister Salahuddin Ahmed on the security arrangements for Durga Puja, a few days ago. He also informed that govt’s Hindu Religious Welfare Trust had increased the grant for puja celebrations to Rs 5cr this year, against the previous year’s grant of Rs 4cr.Meanwhile, another BPUP member said that desecration of idols were reported from at least 11 districts last year. “This time, there’ve been four incidents so far -- in Sylhet, Rajbari, Panchagarh and Tangail districts. And the govt also promptly took necessary legal measures... Law enforcement agencies told us that their personnel will be deployed near the pandals, but organising committees should also have their volunteers to maintain a vigil,” he said, requesting anonymity.Earlier, home minister Ahmed had said: “No security risks have been reported regarding Durga Puja pandals in Bangladesh so far. articles.title: Drone strike kills 30 people in Sudan’s Blue Nile region
articles.summary: Drone reportedly linked to RSF targets Wad al-Mahi, killing dozens near displacement camp, including women and children.
articles.body:
At least 30 displaced people, including women and children, have been killed and dozens of others have been wounded following a drone attack in southeastern Sudan.

The governor of Wad al-Mahi province told Al Jazeera on Friday that a drone belonging to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targeted the centre of the province, killing 26 women and four children.

Governor Mahjoub Al-Sheikh described the attack as “cowardly”. He said the drone was launched from “inside Ethiopia”, according to the AFP news agency.

Al Jazeera Arabic’s Sudan correspondent, Wadah Al-Tahir, explained that the attack was the latest in a wave of drone strikes targeting the Blue Nile region and this time Wad al-Mahi province near the city of Damazin was struck.

Friday’s attack was just outside a displacement camp, near an informal gold mining site, where women earn a daily wage using chemicals and their bare hands to clear gold nuggets from the earth extracted by men.

The latest frontline in the war between the Sudanese army and the RSF is the border region with Ethiopia, which is facing its own internal conflict that threatens to escalate.

Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of harbouring RSF fighters and bases – Ethiopia has denied the allegations.

Local sources say the porous border between the two countries is a key supply line for the paramilitary and its allies, AFP reported.

The RSF launched its offensive towards Damazin but the advance could put the army in a bind, forcing it to defend territory on both the Blue Nile front and in the Kordofan region, where a year of deadly drone strikes has left the two sides deadlocked.

Aid workers estimate that Sudan’s civil war has killed more than 200,000 people since it started in April 2023, creating one of the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

Nearly 100,000 people have been displaced in Blue Nile state this year alone, according to United Nations figures.

articles.title: Thousands flood Brussels streets as anti-austerity protests erupt into clashes with police
articles.summary: Masked agitators clashed with riot police in Brussels as thousands of others marched against Belgium's austerity measures and cost of living crisis.
articles.body: Thousands of demonstrators poured into the streets of Brussels on Friday, at times clashing with police officers, to protest the Belgian government's budget-tightening measures and the overall rise in the cost of living. Dozens of protesters, most of them young and dressed in black with masks over their faces, were seen throwing rocks and firecrackers at police at the central Brussels railway station, The Associated Press reported. They also set several fires, with photos showing a man lighting an electric scooter ablaze. MAY DAY PROTESTS ACROSS EUROPE AND ASIA TURN INTO ANTI-AMERICAN, ANTI-ISRAEL POLITICAL BATTLEGROUNDS Riot police responded by deploying tear gas canisters and shooting water cannons, tactics that dispersed the crowds. The chaos in the streets contributed to increased traffic across the Belgian capital. Police said the unrest was caused by people unaffiliated with the anti-austerity demonstration, which drew an estimated 30,000 participants, the AP reported. Two of Belgium’s largest labor unions organized Friday’s daylong national strike, with a separate public-sector walkout planned for Monday. Union leaders also distanced themselves from the unrest, saying those responsible were not affiliated with their movement. THINK YOUR STATE IS EXPENSIVE? NEW DATA REVEALS WHERE AMERICANS FACE THE HIGHEST COST-OF-LIVING Union members and their supporters were dressed in red or green as they marched peacefully throughout the city. Marie Gobert, a single mother and social worker, came to Brussels from Namur for the march, telling the AP she "cannot make ends meet." The rising cost of schools, public transport and train tickets is what preoccupies her the most. FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE "You can feel the social tension, you can feel anger starting to simmer everywhere," Gobert said. "The education system is being dismantled, and when young people want to speak out, no one listens to them." This summer, Belgium’s French Community government raised standard university tuition by roughly 43% this academic year, from €835 to €1,194, as part of a broader austerity program. This week, hundreds of students took to the streets of the eastern Belgian city of Liège. Local media reported that 107 students were arrested. articles.title: Erika Kirk says presidential library-style tribute to Charlie Kirk is 'in the works' as TPUSA expands
articles.summary: Erika Kirk said a presidential library-style tribute to Charlie Kirk is in the works as TPUSA expands across high school and college campuses.
articles.body: Erika Kirk says plans for a permanent memorial honoring her late husband, Charlie Kirk, are "in the works" as she oversees what the organization describes as Turning Point USA's rapid expansion on high school and college campuses nationwide. "I want to make sure that it's something where our students that are currently in chapters, one day, their children will be chapter leaders or chapter members," Kirk told Fox News' Griff Jenkins. Kirk gave the "Fox & Friends Weekend" co-host an exclusive tour of Turning Point USA's Arizona headquarters in a segment that aired Friday on "Fox & Friends," offering a behind-the-scenes look at the organization's growth and the spaces where she preserves her husband's memory. INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES Kirk also discussed plans for a memorial beyond the existing tributes. When asked whether she could envision building a presidential library-style tribute to her husband, Kirk said the organization was already considering the idea. "It's on our list, and it's something that we have in the works," she said. The proposed tribute would build on memorial displays already housed at Turning Point USA's headquarters, where Kirk has preserved handwritten letters and Bibles sent by supporters, along with personal items her husband left behind. Among the reminders is Charlie Kirk's office, where notes remain on his desk and his chair sits empty. CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING "My kids are the only ones that sit in it," Kirk said. Kirk also said her husband left behind outlines of his vision for Turning Point USA, which she said continues to guide the organization after his death. "I'm just so blessed and grateful that Charlie left with us hundreds of his journals," she said. "He wrote down a lot about the future of Turning Point and the vision of Turning Point." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Turning Point USA says student involvement has increased as the organization expands its presence on high school and college campuses nationwide. "Students were everything to Charlie," Kirk said. "This was his mission ground, was to be able to touch the hearts and minds of the students, and he did that. And through our amazing team that we have, we're continuing to do that."

articles.title: Elon Musk fires another salvo over Starlink delay, targets Ambani again
articles.summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Friday fired another salvo over the delay in the commercial rollout of Starlink in India, taking swipe at billionaire Mukesh
articles.body: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Friday fired another salvo over the delay in the commercial rollout of Starlink in India, taking swipe at billionaire Mukesh Ambani once again.In a post on X, Musk addressed the Reliance Industries chairman as “Prime Minister Ambani”, alleging that he was the “real boss of India” and questioning why Starlink was yet to receive the necessary clearances to begin commercial operations.“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote.He argued that Starlink could improve access to the internet in underserved parts of the country, particularly for children seeking educational opportunities and small businesses looking to reach international markets.“There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. Thank you” he added.Musk's latest remarks come a day after he accused unnamed Indian business groups of obstructing Starlink's entry to protect their market positions. He had alleged that the company was being blocked by “certain oligarchs” seeking to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”.The Indian government has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the delay stems from pending regulatory and security requirements rather than preferential treatment for domestic telecom companies.At the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not permit a monopoly in any sector and that three satellite communication operators had received licences.These include Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink. Amazon's Project Kuiper has also expressed interest in entering the market and will undergo the standard evaluation process.Scindia said the government was finalising the satellite spectrum pricing framework, while security assessments by the Ministry of Home Affairs and other agencies were under way. Commercial operations can begin once the companies meet the prescribed requirements.The government has also said security clearances remain pending for all three licensed operators, rejecting the suggestion that Starlink alone is facing regulatory hurdles.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: U.S. hits International Criminal Court with sweeping sanctions, hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize
articles.summary: The Trump administration has imposed sweeping new sanctions on the International Criminal Court as part of its campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into the United States and its allies, including Israel.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration has imposed sweeping new sanctions on the International Criminal Court as part of its campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into the United States and its allies, including Israel. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the sanctions Friday, after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African jurist Navi Pillay, a former judge at the ICC and other international courts. Trump has coveted that prize for himself. “We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate against us,” Rubio said in a video address posted to social media. “The United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC.” The sanctions cut the court off from U.S.-based financial services, technology companies and even using U.S. dollars. They set a six-month timeline for U.S. companies and individuals that have business with the court to wind that business down. The ICC denounced the step as an attack on the rule of law and the foundations of international order, themes that Rubio had appeared to embrace only two days ago in a speech in front of the Acropolis in Athens. “It is an attempt to obstruct the course of justice and to prevent the court from doing what it was created to do,” the court said in a statement. “It is an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order which strikes at the simple principle that no one stands above the law.” ICC President Tomoko Akane, a citizen of U.S. ally Japan, said the court would “continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes.” She also appealed to other ICC members for support. “This is not just about defending a single institution, but about safeguarding the international order grounded upon the rule of law.” Rights groups also denounced the sanctions. “This existential attack must fail,” said Erika Guevara Rosas, an Amnesty International senior director. “States must take concrete action to resist the imposition of these measures and actively protect the Court.” The court’s host country of the Netherlands has been preparing for weeks for the move. One possible measure to mitigate sanctions is the EU “blocking statute,” which could be used to protect European court staff by preventing European companies from complying with the U.S. measures. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has called the blocking statute the “nuclear option” in countering possible sanctions, but said the Netherlands has been in talks with the European Commission to ensure that if it is necessary it can be quickly enacted. In a joint statement, Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom expressed strong disagreement with the U.S. sanctions. “We will continue to work together to support the court’s vital work, uphold the rules-based international system, and advance accountability,” the statement said. “If put into effect, these sanctions will have a significant impact on the court’s work, its dedicated staff and their families. They work every day to bring those accused of the most serious international crimes to justice and to support their victims.” Rubio said U.S. allies should join in the U.S. actions. “If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, piece by piece, until Americans are threatened no longer,” he said. A number of countries have withdrawn from the court this year, including Venezuela and Chad. The South Pacific island nation of Naoero was the most recent to announce it would quit.

articles.title: Who is Navi Pillay? Nobel Peace Prize winner's UN record renews fierce antisemitism accusations
articles.summary: Navi Pillay's 2026 Nobel Peace Prize sparked backlash from Jewish advocacy groups and UN Watch over allegations of anti-Israel bias and antisemitism.
articles.body: The decision to award the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to former U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay sparked fierce backlash Friday from Jewish advocacy groups and U.N. watchdogs accusing the South African jurist of longstanding anti-Israel bias and defending antisemitic rhetoric. The Norwegian Nobel Committee honored Pillay, 85, for her contributions to international law and efforts to hold perpetrators of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide accountable. But her selection immediately reignited controversies surrounding her leadership of U.N. investigations into Israel, her defense of a fellow commissioner accused of antisemitism and positions she expressed before being appointed to investigate the Jewish state. Bayefsky accused Pillay of having "perfected the art of perverting legal and universal standards of human rights to demonize and delegitimize Jewish self-determination. This award stands as a testament to human wrongs." The Nobel Committee offered a sharply different assessment of Pillay's legacy, praising her lifelong commitment to international justice and describing her career as an example of courage and integrity in defending the rule of law. ISRAEL VINDICATED BY GAZA NUTRITION DATA AFTER ‘BLOOD LIBEL’ STARVATION CLAIMS, UN ENVOY SAYS Who Is Navi Pillay? Born in Durban, South Africa, in 1941, Pillay built her career challenging apartheid-era discrimination, becoming the first non-White woman appointed to South Africa's high court. She later served as a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. From 2008 to 2014, she served as U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights. In 2021, she was appointed to chair the U.N. Human Rights Council's open-ended Commission of Inquiry investigating alleged violations in Israel and the Palestinian territories. In September 2025, the commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a finding Israel rejected as politically motivated and biased. The commission's conclusion was not a ruling by an international court. Geneva-based UN Watch condemned Friday's Nobel announcement, accusing Pillay of breaching the impartiality expected of international investigators. UN CHIEF BACKS OFFICIAL WHO REPOSTED ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVIST'S CLAIMS AMID CALLS FOR INVESTIGATION "We are shocked that the Nobel Committee honored Navi Pillay," Executive Director Hillel Neuer said. "Her troubling record on antisemitism and gross breach of ethics in presiding over a notorious U.N. commission utterly disqualifies her from such an award." Neuer pointed to a June 2020 manifesto that Pillay signed calling on governments to "Sanction Apartheid Israel," along with a June 2021 letter urging President Joe Biden to punish Israel after its conflict with Hamas. UN Watch argued that the positions raised questions about her impartiality before she accepted the commission's chairmanship in July 2021. Despite the criticism, U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres congratulated Pillay on receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, praising her decades-long career in international justice and specifically highlighting her leadership of the U.N. investigation into Israel. "For decades, she has been a champion of international law and human rights and a steadfast, independent voice of justice amidst some of the most historic international legal cases of our time," Guterres said in a statement on Friday. NORWAY FACES BACKLASH OVER 'DEEPLY RACIST' PROPOSAL TO JAIL CITIZENS FOR WEST BANK BUSINESS Another controversy erupted in 2022 when fellow commissioner Miloon Kothari suggested that social media criticism of the investigation was controlled by the "Jewish lobby" and questioned Israel's U.N. membership. The controversy also reached Germany, where Berlin's mayor withdrew support for a planned event honoring Pillay in 2022, and the event was canceled, according to The Times of Israel. Bayefsky also recalled the 2009 U.N. anti-racism conference in Geneva, when Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad delivered an inflammatory speech attacking Israel. "Her after-the-fact denunciation was utterly disingenuous." Bayefsky claimed, "Pillay had been given Ahmadinejad’s speech, questioning the veracity of the Holocaust and talking about the "ugly faces" of Zionists, in advance and yet still handed him the microphone as Conference Secretary-General." The Nobel Committee, meanwhile, defended Pillay's legacy, crediting her with strengthening international law at a time when the institutions responsible for enforcing it face increasing political pressure. articles.title: Gaza ceasefire ‘exists in name only’, more than 100 NGOs say
articles.summary: Humanitarian and human rights groups call out Israel’s continued killings and restrictions across the enclave.
articles.body:
One year after the so-called ceasefire in Gaza was reached with United States backing, it exists only on paper, according to more than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil society organisations.

“The ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily, and restrictions on aid, equipment and rebuilding materials preventing families from recovering,” a joint statement by the NGOs said on Friday.

Amnesty International, the Norwegian Refugee Council, Save the Children, Oxfam, Greenpeace and dozens of other international groups said Israeli attacks in the enclave have killed more than 1,400 Palestinians, including at least 327 children, in the year since US President Trump announced a deal to end hostilities as part of the Gaza Board of Peace framework.

“It is utterly shameful that a full year after the ceasefire was signed, so little has improved for Palestinians in Gaza,” Jan Egeland, secretary-general of the Norwegian Refugee Council, said in the joint statement.

Inger Ashing, chief executive of Save the Children, said, “A ceasefire is meaningless if children are still being killed and families are still unable to rebuild their lives.”

He noted that since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire was announced, “nearly one child has been killed every day.”

In the three years since Israel’s October 2023 genocidal war began, more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed and 175,000 others wounded – about one in every 13 people in Gaza – according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

A conservative World Health Organization (WHO) estimate suggests roughly 24 percent of the wounded have life-changing injuries requiring long-term rehabilitation, a quarter of them children.

Gaza’s few remaining health facilities are overwhelmed and have dwindling supplies, and none of its 36 hospitals is operating at full capacity, with widespread shortages of medicine, equipment and fuel, Friday’s ministry statement said.

It said that more than 18,500 patients, including at least 4,000 children, need medical evacuation, and more than 1,000 have died while waiting.

Almost 2 million Palestinians in the enclave are also in desperate need of shelter, where 80 percent of structures are damaged, the statement said.

Norwegian Refugee Council’s Egeland warned that restrictions on equipment and construction materials continue to prevent recovery.

“Israeli restrictions are still preventing the required equipment or materials, which are the only ways for communities to begin rebuilding their lives,” he said.

At the same time, 1.4 million people in Gaza are “facing crisis-level hunger or worse through the end of the year”, the statement added.

On Friday in Gaza, Israeli forces shot dead at least one Palestinian after firing live ammunition at civilians in the al-Musaddar, Maghazi and Bureij refugee camp areas in the centre of the Strip, which also came under heavy Israeli artillery shelling.

In Khan Younis in the south, Israeli tanks directed heavy fire towards the Bani Suheila roundabout, where a number of injuries were reported.

On Thursday, at least eight Palestinians were killed and dozens injured in Israeli air strikes and shelling across Gaza.

Friday’s statement noted that Israeli forces had further squeezed the Palestinian population into an even more crowded environment by arbitrarily moving the so-called “Yellow Line”, established as a buffer to separate Israeli-controlled areas and the Palestinians as part of last year’s ceasefire framework.

The “ceasefire” took effect on October 10, 2025. Since then, Israel has killed at least 1,471 Palestinians and injured 5,189.

Three years of Israeli attacks have killed at least 74,254 Palestinians, including at least 21,000 children. That is about one in every 30 people, or 3 percent of the pre-war population.

The Palestinian Ministry of Health counts only deaths recorded at hospitals or officially registered. The true toll is likely much higher, as it excludes the thousands still buried in destroyed buildings or missing.

“Accountability cannot be buried under the rubble,” Agnes Callamard, the secretary-general of Amnesty International, said in the joint statement. “The persistent failure to hold Israel accountable and press Israel to comply with the International Court of Justice’s binding orders continues to fuel the atrocity crimes on a mass scale against Palestinians.”

articles.title: Federal judge blocks deportation of Dominican illegal immigrant shot by ICE during NYC arrest attempt

articles.body: A federal judge has temporarily blocked the deportation of an illegal immigrant who was shot Thursday during a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operation in New York City. In a two-page order, U.S. District Judge Paul Oetken, an Obama appointee, ruled that the man — whom police identified as Oscar Belgal but who was named in a court document as Oscar Bergal — cannot be removed from the United States without a court order while his petition challenging his detention remains pending. The judge also barred federal authorities from transferring him to any facility outside the Southern or Eastern Districts of New York or the District of New Jersey without prior court approval. MAMDANI DEMANDS TRUMP RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE AGENT AS PROTESTS ERUPT IN THE BRONX In a Friday court hearing, a judge dismissed a defense application for a temporary restringing order with prejudice because federal prosecutors didn't challenge Oetken's order that Belgal not be deported. Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican national, was shot after refusing to comply with lawful orders while ICE officers were conducting a targeted operation to arrest him in the Bronx, according to the Department of Homeland Security. During the encounter, the Belgal pulled his vehicle forward before at least one officer fired seven rounds, striking him below his left ear, NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at a news conference near the shooting scene late Thursday. ICE officers used their vehicles to block him as he attempted to drive away, but Belgal accelerated toward them, Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, said Friday during a news conference in Washington alongside DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. "Our officers, using their training and believing that their life and the life of the partners and the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," Charles said. AUSTIN ICE SHOOTING SPARKS FIGHT OVER VENEZUELAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT'S DEPORTATION A 5-year-old boy inside the vehicle was unharmed. In a statement, Bronx District Attorney Darcel Clark said her office was working to establish the facts of the case and determine the next course of action. Outside the courthouse, Harold Solis, an immigration attorney with the nonprofit Make the Road New York, criticized the ICE officers' actions. articles.title: ‘Barbaric’: US lawmakers condemn plan to livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution
articles.summary: Republican and Democratic lawmakers condemn Pentagon plan to livestream Fort Hood shooter’s execution by firing squad.
articles.body:
United States Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has received widespread condemnation over his announcement to livestream the execution of a man who killed 13 people at a military base in Texas.

Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle in the US Congress were quick to react in the hours after the Pentagon chief told a conservative news outlet on Thursday that former US Army Major Nidal Hasan’s death by firing squad would be made public.

“Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting”, Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who recently expressed regret for his 2025 vote to confirm Hegseth to lead the Department of Defense, said on social media. “Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America.”

Republican Congressman Austin Scott, who serves on the US House Armed Services Committee, also opposed the announcement.

“I absolutely support the sentence of death, but live-streaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that,” the Georgia lawmaker said on X.

Scott’s Republican colleague in the US House, Congressman Rob Bresnahan, said, “The focus should be on justice for the victims and their families.”

“Their pain deserves respect, not a public show,” Bresnahan said.

Al Jazeera has not heard back from the three Republican senators – Susan Collins, Mitch McConnell and Lisa Murkowski – who opposed Hegseth’s confirmation.

Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was sentenced to death in August 2013 after a military jury found him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted murder for the shooting at Fort Hood.

On Monday, US President Donald Trump authorised the use of a firing squad in Hasan’s execution. Hegseth said Thursday that it would take place at the military base on December 3 at 1pm local time (19:00 GMT), the same time the 2009 shooting took place.

Later on Friday, Trump confirmed he “absolutely” approved of the execution of the Fort Hood shooter but said he had not made a determination on showing the death via livestream.

US Senator Jack Reed, who serves as the top Democrat on the US Senate Armed Services Committee, called on the Trump administration on Friday to “reconsider” the decision, saying it is a “gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters”.

“Live-streaming an execution is a barbaric spectacle,” the Rhode Island lawmaker told Al Jazeera in a statement. “This is yet another stunt by Secretary Hegseth to distract from his tenure’s repeated failings which have only weakened our national security and standing in the world”.

Reed added, “It is absolutely shameful and damaging to America’s interests and core values.”

His fellow Democrat, Senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut, rolled his eyes and appeared visibly shocked during a CNN interview on Thursday when asked about Hegseth’s decision.

“That’s disgusting”, Murphy told CNN’s Erin Burnett. “Is he mimicking ISIS [ISIL] executions? I understand that, in this country, we have the death penalty, but public executions [are] medieval”.

But not every lawmaker is opposed to the idea.

Republican Congressman Andy Ogles of Tennessee said on social media that “public execution is what this terrorist deserves”, calling Hegseth’s decision “excellent”.

US Vice President JD Vance, during a trip to his home state of Ohio on Friday, told reporters he won’t “be watching” the livestream of Hasan’s death.

“I see these announcements. I don’t know that that’s actually going to happen”, Vance, who served in the US Marine Corps, said. “Let’s sort of see … when he’s executed.”

US Army policy limits who may witness military executions. According to regulation issued by the military branch, no person under the age of 18 may witness an execution. Victims, their family members, the prisoner’s lawyer and at least two members of the news media are among the limited number of people who are allowed to view.

For Hasan’s execution to be “public”, Reed said Trump would have to approve a waiver.

When asked whether Trump would grant that permission, the White House referred Al Jazeera to the Pentagon.

The head of the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which regulates broadcast communications in the country, said on Friday he would defer to the Pentagon on whether US networks could air the execution.

“Ultimately, we’re going to defer to Secretary Hegseth and, you know, his decisions on how to move forward with this,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a CNBC interview.

An official at the Defense Department told Al Jazeera that the agency has “nothing additional to provide”.

The United Nations has strongly condemned the livestreaming of Hasan’s execution, stating that it would breach international law.

A spokesperson for the UN human rights office told the news agency AFP that broadcasting the execution would be “tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture”.

articles.title: Powerful earthquake shakes Panama
articles.summary: A major earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.7 has struck Panama, according to the US Geological Survey.
articles.body: A major earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.7 has struck southern Panama, according to the US Geological Survey. Several people have suffered minor injuries but so far there are no reports of fatalities, officials said. The USGS had said some casualties were possible and extensive damage was probable. Footage verified by CNN shows several damaged buildings in Penonome, some 70 miles from the epicenter. One video shows a church with a partially collapsed steeple and another building with a crumbled facade. In the popular resort town Playa Venao, a multi-story building collapsed and crushed several cars beneath it. Along the Panama Canal, the Centennial Bridge’s suspension cables were seen shaking as vehicles drove through. The canal’s authority said operations were continuing as normal and that staff were inspecting facilities for potential damage. Panama City’s public transit system has suspended service on two metro lines and evacuated passengers from some stations. The Education Ministry has canceled classes nationwide for the rest of the day. Panama’s main international airport has been temporarily closed as a precaution and flights have been diverted to other airports, the civil aviation authority said. The water and sewage institute has reported interruptions at several water treatment plants due to power outages caused by the quake. Panama’s President José Raúl Mulino has called for calm and instructed the minister of government to provide information on the earthquake’s effects. He has also mobilized resources to those affected. Officials have reported more than 40 aftershocks, including one with a preliminary magnitude of 6.6, according to USGS. Earlier, the US Tsunami Warning System warned of possible tsunami waves along some coasts before saying there was no longer a threat. This is the latest powerful earthquake to have struck Latin America this year. Over the summer, Venezuela was hit by two powerful earthquakes that killed more than 6,400 people, while Colombia suffered a tremor that left around 300 dead. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: In 1937, a Florida family started a cattle ranch; nearly 90 years later, Adams Ranch spans 50,000 acres, ranks among the country's largest cow-calf operations and raises its fifth generation
articles.summary: What began as a small cattle operation in Florida in 1937 has grown into a sprawling ranch spanning approximately 50,000 acres across several counties.
articles.body: What began as a small cattle operation in Florida in 1937 has grown into a sprawling ranch spanning approximately 50,000 acres across several counties. At Adams Ranch in Fort Pierce, four generations of the same family have worked the land, and a fifth generation is now growing up amid the cattle, open pastures and traditions that have defined the family business for nearly nine decades.Founded by the grandfather of current ranch president Mike Adams, the ranch has grown into one of the country's largest cow-calf operations. Yet, despite the expansion of cities and residential developments across Florida, much of daily life at Adams Ranch continues to follow the rhythms established generations ago.A family tradition that began in 1937“The ranch was started in 1937 by my grandfather,” Mike Adams told CBS 12 News, reflecting on the family's long history in cattle ranching.For ranch foreman Billy Adams, the connection to the land began when he was a child. “I started here when I was five years old,” he recalled.Today, the ranch continues to operate through hands-on work, with cowboys riding horses to move cattle between pastures and herding dogs helping guide the animals. The workday begins early, often before sunrise, reflecting the demanding routine that comes with managing a large cattle operation.For Billy, ranching is not simply an occupation but a way of life that has shaped his understanding of family and hard work.“It's just a way of life,” he said. “And it's a good way of life. Good way to bring up your family.”Preserving the memories of generations pastThe history of Adams Ranch can be seen throughout the property, where family photographs and old artifacts document the lives of those who helped establish and maintain the operation.The ranch also houses a museum featuring objects collected on the property over the years. The collection offers a glimpse into an older Florida, preserving memories of a time when vast stretches of open land and cattle ranches played a more visible role in the state's landscape.For the Adams family, maintaining these records is a way of ensuring that the generations who came before them are not forgotten. Their story also reflects a broader chapter of Florida's history, one that continues even as the state undergoes rapid change.Development puts pressure on Florida's ranch landWhile new homes, businesses and other developments continue to spread across Florida, the family says the expansion is putting pressure on the land available for traditional ranching.“It's squeezing some of the land in a lot of different areas of Florida,” Mike Adams said.The family sees preserving ranch land as important not only for the future of cattle ranching but also for maintaining open spaces, supporting wildlife and protecting the state's natural landscape.Food production is another concern. The family believes Florida should retain the ability to produce food for its own residents rather than become increasingly dependent on supplies from elsewhere.“We really do not want to become in a position where we don't provide our own food for our people,” Adams said.Adams Ranch also sells its own beef directly to the community, maintaining a connection between the operation and local consumers.Raising the fifth generation on the ranchAfter nearly 90 years, the ranch remains under the hands-on management of the Adams family. Its continued operation reflects the work of generations who have maintained the land and passed their knowledge down to their children and grandchildren.For Billy Adams, the lessons learned on the ranch have stayed with him throughout his life.“It taught me that hard work won't kill you,” he said.The family is now raising the fifth generation on the property, with hopes that the children will continue the traditions that have sustained the operation since its founding. articles.title: Florida commissioners unanimously rejected development across nearly 230 acres in 2025; 16 months later, they reversed course 4-3 and approved more than 4,800 apartments and about 1,000 hotel rooms
articles.summary: Orange County commissioners in Florida have approved the large Tuscana land-use plan in a close 4-3 vote.
articles.body: Orange County commissioners in Florida have approved the large Tuscana land-use plan in a close 4-3 vote. The decision reverses a unanimous rejection of the same project 16 months earlier. The approval allows more than 4,800 apartments and about 1,000 hotel rooms to be built across nearly 230 acres in the Shingle Creek Basin. Nearby homeowners say they fear the high-density project will cause serious flooding, destroy wildlife habitats, and put too much pressure on local roads. In May 2025, county commissioners unanimously rejected the proposal because of environmental concerns. But the decision was later reviewed after an independent Special Magistrate examined the case under state land-use rules and formally recommended that the commission reconsider its original decision.Legal pressures and magistrate findingsThe push to reconsider the application grew after the magistrate found that the county's earlier rejection was not supported by competent, substantial evidence. According to local news outlet WKMG ClickOrlando, several commissioners who supported the project during the latest hearing said they were worried about possible financial risks if the landowners sued the county. The development site covers nearly 230 acres between Central Florida Parkway and State Road 417. The area includes nearly 59 acres of sensitive wetlands in the headwaters of the Florida Everglades system. After the vote, attorney S. William "Bill" Moore of Moore, Bowman & Reese issued a public statement on behalf of developer Shingle Creek Co-Owners LLC. Moore welcomed the decision. He said 176 individual property owners had spent years going through public review for land that the county had long designated for high-density use. The developer said the project was carefully planned to address environmental concerns while protecting private property rights. The approved plans include larger wetland buffers, partly raised access roads, and specific infrastructure measures designed to reduce possible drainage and flooding problems.Residents express anger over wildlife lossDespite those plans, people living next to the basin quickly expressed disappointment with the board's decision. Local homeowners told WKMG ClickOrlando that turning open land into a developed commercial and residential area would change the natural character of their neighborhood. One resident said the area's large deer population and other wildlife were the main reasons they had bought their home there. Another homeowner said they were worried about the size of the development. They described the commission's vote as alarming and said losing the natural basin would also mean losing an important part of the community's identity. Supporters of the project, including Shingle Creek Co-Owners LLC and Geyer Development LLC, say the development will bring major financial benefits to the region. Corporate filings given to the board say the project will create thousands of local jobs when fully built and will add more than $600 million (£450 million) each year to the local economy.Community activists seek political remedyOpponents say the fight over the Shingle Creek Basin is not over. Community groups are now looking to upcoming local elections as a way to challenge the board's decision before construction can begin. Lee Perry, who represents local advocacy group Protect Shingle Creek, told WKMG ClickOrlando that organizers plan to meet directly with candidates seeking seats on the Orange County Commission. Perry said that because the area is currently in an election cycle, a new county commission board could legally reverse decisions made by the current board. articles.title: Panama earthquake: Tsunami warnings issued after magnitude 7.7 quake
articles.summary: Countries including Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Guatemala and Chile have received warnings after the quake.
articles.body:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake has hit southern Panama, triggering tsunami warnings across Central and South America.

The US National Weather Service issued tsunami warnings for Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Nicaragua and Guatemala on Friday following the quake.

Chile’s naval Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service also issued a tsunami warning.

The US Geological Survey said the earthquake was centred about 10km (6 miles) southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba along the Pacific Ocean coast.

Residents of Panama City reported feeling tremors, with buildings shaking and people evacuating into the streets.

“We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but we’re okay, though we’re very scared,” 60-year-old Rosendo Dominguez, who is from Herrera province, where the earthquake struck, told The Associated Press news agency by phone.

“Everyone is outside, scared,” Dominguez added.

Videos shared by newspaper La Prensa showed the tower of a historic building had collapsed along with several balconies of a residential building in Penonome, a city about halfway between the epicenter and Panama City.

Panama’s ministry of ⁠education ordered schools closed, while President Jose Raul Mulino called for calm

“What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder,” he wrote on X.

There have been several destructive earthquakes in the region this year.

In June, twin quakes hit northern Venezuela, causing widespread devastation and killing at least 6,500 people.

In August, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake hit Colombia, killing at least 289 people.
